memory_update.text: SPSC is the cleanest direct public candidate for the supplier product-data / retail compliance node because it combines retail trading-partner network, item/assortment data, EDI, supplier onboarding, and deduction/chargeback recovery.
DSGX is a strong adjacent underfollowed candidate for tariff, customs, HS classification, denied-party screening, and global trade intelligence workflows tied to consumer import complexity.
ULS and ZBRA are useful reference/adjacent names rather than pure plays: ULS maps to certification and product compliance assets; ZBRA maps to barcode/RFID/labeling infrastructure.

Key private or no-longer-standalone assets in this node include Salsify, 1WorldSync, Trace One, Loftware, Avalara trade compliance, and E2open; public-market mapping may therefore require indirect exposures or acquirer screens.

Next layer should quantify retail/importer exposure and recurring revenue sensitivity for SPSC and DSGX, then test whether tariff volatility is accelerating or delaying supplier compliance software spend.

node: Supplier product-data, item-master, labeling, tariff, and compliance workflow tools
summary: Expanded the universe around retail supplier data/compliance workflows into two lanes: SPS Commerce and Descartes as the most direct public software/data platforms, plus UL Solutions and Zebra Technologies as adjacent compliance/certification and labeling infrastructure anchors. The underfollowed lane is strongest for SPS Commerce and Descartes because they are vertical workflow/data names that may screen as supply-chain software rather than consumer beneficiaries. E2open would have been a direct candidate but is excluded as a current standalone US-listed equity because WiseTech completed its acquisition.
